06/09/2025
Claim opened after a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured driver, who is named on the policy. The
claimant, who is not represented by counsel, reported a knee injury at the scene.
06/28/2025
Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle and that the collision happened
as described. The other driver's statement mtaches the account given to us.
07/22/2025
Photos taken at the scene were reviewed. The damage is mostly in line with the described impact, and nothing
suggests the damage happened before the coverage start date.
09/09/2025
Vehicle history shows no earlier damage on record. The claimant's medical records show no prior injury to the same
knee.
01/01/2026
The claimant later added a few small details about the sequence of events, but the core account stayed the same
across each conversation. Reported injury appears consistent with the kind and force of the crash.
01/02/2026
Treatment followed a usual course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits. Treatment tapered off as the claimant's
knee improved and the provider noted steady recovery.
01/20/2026
Based on the consistent accounts, scene photos, and medical timeline, the claim is proceeding through standard
evaluation with no open questions on liability or causation.
</page>

List the facts written on this page. Copy each value exactly as it is written: same spelling,
punctuation and date format. Do not add anything that is not on this page. Use "" for a missing value.

Person "role" must be one of: claimant, attorney, defense_attorney, expert, doctor, officer, adjuster, witness, other.
  claimant = the person who made the claim (also called patient, plaintiff, client, customer,
  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
